Hi Olivia — thanks for the note and the template. High level answers below and a couple of asks to speed Procure/Finance onboarding.

- PO acceptance: Yes, we can accept a PO that references our standard MSA and the SOW. We typically require the PO to reference Redwood's order form/quote ID (see attached Redwood_Quote_ClearSky_2026-02.pdf) so it maps cleanly to our billing system.

- Payment terms / cadence: Our standard commercial is Net 45. We can invoice monthly in arrears (invoices generated on the 1st of the month for prior month usage). If ClearSky requires quarterly invoicing, we can support that but it will change the invoicing cadence in our system; prefer monthly in arrears for usage visibility.

- Discounts: We can do an 8% platform discount on a 12-month committed spend. If the customer prepays annual fees up-front we can extend to 12%. We also have a Dedicated capacity pricing profile in the SOW if you want predictable unit economics for the pilot -> prod ramp.

- Onboarding docs: For procurement we will provide legal name, Redwood Inference, Inc.; Tax ID: XX-XXXXXXX; remit to (ACH) instructions and a W-9. I've looped Neha in to own the vendor forms and banking details.

Next steps: I'll attach the quote and current SOW draft (Redwood_Dedicated_SOW_v2.pdf). Marissa, can you confirm whether Sales Ops needs a PO number before DocuSign or we can sign SOW and accept PO after?

Rishi / Olivia — quick follow from procurement review. A few points:

- ClearSky standard internal policy is Net 60 for external vendors. We can make exceptions but require Procurement Ops sign-off.
- We prefer quarterly invoices (we consolidate billing across 10+ vendor teams). Monthly invoices add administrative cost for us.
- PO must reference an approved SOW and our internal SLA versioning (we pulled the 3.1 SLA from the attachment).

Can Redwood accept Net 60 and quarterly invoices, or alternatively, accept Net 45 provided the PO references the signed SOW and the vendor onboarding form is complete? Also: we need Redwood's tax ID on the PO.

Subject: ClearSky procurement — recommended commercial compromise and ask for Sales Ops approval

Team,

Summary of the procurement ask: ClearSky is pushing Net 60 + quarterly invoicing. Procurement will route faster if we accept Net 60, but that increases receivable duration and cash impact. They're open to Net 45 if the PO references a signed SOW and we provide the vendor onboarding data quickly.

Suggested compromise (recommend we approve):
- Accept PO with Net 45 and monthly invoices in arrears, provided:
  - SOW is signed and references the Redwood quote ID RDW-2387,
  - ClearSky references our legal name and tax ID on the PO,
  - They complete onboarding form and remit-to bank details are captured in our portal.
- Commercial sweetener: offer 10% standard discount on 12-month committed spend (8% baseline, bump to 10% as one-time concession) OR 12% for prepaid annual. We should avoid deeper discounting given Dedicated capacity margin.

Operational asks:
- Marissa: please confirm Sales Ops can accept a PO number post-signature (i.e., sign SOW via DocuSign, then attach incoming PO to the order) or do we need the PO up front?
- Neha: please prepare W-9, tax ID, and ACH remit instructions to send to procurement once Marissa confirms.
- Karthik: ping me if we need to adjust SOW MLOps hours for dedicated pilot to keep overall TCV within the committed discount band.

I'm copying procurement so we can close this quickly — ClearSky wants to route the PO this week if we can confirm the above. If Procurement insists on Net 60, come back here and I'll request a revenue holdback or short-term credit card/stripe billing as an exception.

Thanks,
Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
